name: audio-quiet-counterfactual
description: THE MIRROR: QUIET's expectations, SATURATE's boot key. Must FAIL.  Generated by pokemon/tools/make_audio.py --specs; do not hand-edit. Expected red: arm, maxactive, slotmask, steals, steals_sounding, stealmask. Expected green: the other eleven.

probes.why: Which arm the boot key selected. A spec that asserts a steal count without asserting WHICH run produced it is a number about an unknown situation (doc 69).
gSoundInfo.maxChans, read back out of the live driver. This is the wall itself: m4aSoundInit passes (5 << SOUND_MODE_MAXCHN_SHIFT) into an array of 12.
NUM_MUSIC_PLAYERS. It is ((u16)gNumMusicPlayers), a LINKER ABSOLUTE whose address is the value -- which is why grepping src/ and sound/ for it finds nothing.
The most channels ever SF_ON at one time, latched. The load-bearing observation: however many claimants arrive, this cannot exceed maxChans.
Every channel index ever seen SF_ON, one bit each. Channels 5 through 11 exist, are allocated, are 64 bytes each, and can never be reached -- the mask is what says so.
ClearChain calls arriving on a PCM channel that is SF_ON. The other two ClearChain sites in m4a_1.s both test SF_ON and call only when it is CLEAR, so this counts the victim walk at :1721 exactly.
The subset of steals that took a channel WITHOUT SF_STOP -- a note still sounding rather than one already releasing. This is the cut you can hear.
Which channel indices were stolen from. A count says the budget ran out; the mask says where.
SetPokemonCryTone calls that found NO free cry player and fell through to maxClockIndex, restarting a player that was still running. Counted at the fallthrough itself, not inferred.
Two bits per cry, oldest in bits 0-1: which player each cry landed on. With two players the third cry must repeat an index, and the log is what shows the repeat.
How many burst items this arm actually fired. Doc 73's rule: when a feature reads as completely missing, suspect a consumed input or a path never reached before a dead code path.
gAudioProbeOffsets[0] = sizeof(struct SoundChannel), published by the compiler. A hand-derivation during doc 76 came out at 44 by missing every pointer field.
gAudioProbeOffsets[9] = SOUND_CHANNEL_SF_ON, the mask the allocator itself tests.
gAudioProbeOffsets[6] = MAX_DIRECTSOUND_CHANNELS. The array bound, against maxchans which is the usable part of it.
Doc 66's rule -- assert that the thing under test actually happened. A channel table read outside the overworld is a measurement of a different screen.

assert.why: The run ended in the overworld, so every latch above was filled by the arm this spec names.
The boot key selected this arm. Non-zero for every arm on purpose -- doc 58's rule that an exact compare against zero survives an address shift.
THE WALL. m4aSoundInit configures 5 simultaneous PCM voices, read back out of the running driver rather than out of the source.
MAX_DIRECTSOUND_CHANNELS is 12, so 7 channels are allocated and unreachable.

NUM_MUSIC_PLAYERS is 4, and doc 76 section 5 left this unestablished. It is a LINKER ABSOLUTE (ld_script.ld: gNumMusicPlayers = 4;) whose address is the number, which is why no C file defines it. Read here out of the running game.
sizeof(struct SoundChannel), published by the compiler. Doc 76's hand-derivation said 44.
SOUND_CHANNEL_SF_ON = START|STOP|IEC|ENV. The mask the allocator's `tst` tests, so the detector tests the same one.
Every burst item this arm declares actually fired. A zero here would mean the arm never ran, which reads exactly like a working ceiling.
THE LOAD-BEARING ONE. However many claimants arrive, the mixer never has more than maxChans voices going.
Every channel index ever used, one bit each.
ClearChain on an SF_ON PCM channel: the victim walk.  SUPPORTING: an exact compare against zero survives an address shift (doc 58).
Steals that cut a note that was still sounding.  SUPPORTING: an exact compare against zero survives an address shift (doc 58).
Which channel indices got stolen from.  SUPPORTING: an exact compare against zero survives an address shift (doc 58).
Cries that had to evict a running cry player.  SUPPORTING: an exact compare against zero survives an address shift (doc 58).
Two bits per cry: which player each landed on.
